To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the offset-apertured probe is capable of providing high energy throughput and high spatial resolution, (ii) the energy throughput is a strong function of the offset distance and the aperture size, (iii) the energy throughput increases with increasing wavelength, (iv) the energy throughput decreases with increasing NA, and (v) the energy throughput and the lateral resolution increase with increasing NA.

(i) the energy throughput of the aperture is not affected by the offset, but the energy throughput of scattering-type probes is; (ii) the resolution of the aperture is affected by the offset and is degraded by the presence of the scattering-type probe.
the offset-aperture probe can achieve higher throughput than the conventional probe and that its lateral resolution can be improved by increasing the offset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of near-field scanning optical microscopes (NSOM).
the development of a new type of scanning optical probe that is a hybrid between a scattering-type probe and an apertured probe.
the development of a novel NSOM probe that can be used to obtain both far-field and near-field information on a sample.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the offset aperture probe is a hybrid aperture/scattering probe that has the advantages of the aperture probe and the scattering probe, while having a much higher energy throughput than the aperture probe.
the offset-apertured probe is a hybrid apertured and scattering-type NSOM probe.
the offset-apertured probe has a higher energy throughput and resolution than a conventional apertured probe, but is more sensitive to the tip radius and offset than a scattering-type probe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the offset-aperture NSOM probe has an energy throughput comparable to a conventional aperture probe, and a resolution comparable to a scattering-type probe.
a hybrid NSOM probe, which combines the aperture-type and the scattering-type probes, is a promising candidate for the development of a high resolution NSOM system.
a subwavelength offset-apertured probe can be a viable alternative to a conventional aperture-type probe.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a hybrid apertured and scattering-type NSOM tip can be designed to have a high energy throughput and a sub-wavelength resolution, and that the energy throughput can be improved by increasing the offset distance between the aperture and the apex.
the aperture offset can be exploited to enhance the energy throughput of the NSOM probe while maintaining a resolution on par with that of a conventional aperture probe.
a hybrid NSOM probe can be made that has a higher energy throughput than the standard aperture-type probe while still retaining the resolution of a scattering-type probe.
